panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Chest CT panel from a glanders case report showing hilar lymphadenomegaly and segmental compressive atelectasis; these specific findings are not in the provided vocabulary, but the panel is a real patient image from the glanders case and supports pulmonary involvement. B: Axial chest CT from a confirmed glanders case showing bilateral pleural effusion, a recognized glanders manifestation, with basal consolidations and pericardial effusion; caption and in-text support pleural effusion/pneumonia in the patient. C: Chest CT from a glanders case showing peripheral nodular opacities and subpleural consolidations; no exact matching vocabulary term, but the panel is a real patient image supporting pulmonary glanders. D: Chest CT from a glanders case showing bilateral ground-glass opacities and consolidations due to pulmonary inflammation; no exact vocabulary term, but real patient image from the glanders case.
panels.attribution_text: dos Santos et al. Clinical repercussions of Glanders (Burkholderia mallei infection) in a Brazilian child: a case report.. Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical 2020. doi:10.1590/0037-8682-0054-2020. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2:.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Hilar lymphadenomegaly associated with segmental compressive atelectasis on the left side. (B) Bilateral pleural effusion with basal consolidations and pericardial effusion. (C) Peripheral nodular opacities in the pulmonary apices, some subpleural confluent forming consolidations. (D) Bilateral ground-glass opacities and consolidations associated with inflammation in both lungs.
in_text_mentions: The patient underwent significant clinical worsening; in addition to shock (was given vasoactive drugs), he experienced pericardial effusion and pneumonia with bilateral pleural effusion, (observed using chest computed tomography) (Figure 2).
